Three promises

Current evidence, demonstrations, and capability requirements.

Security claims on this page are scoped to named implementations and evidence. Browser self-tests demonstrate primitives, not every daemon path, deployment, endpoint, or provider boundary.

No account required.

No email address or phone number is required to create a local device identity. Peers and network infrastructure can still observe the connection metadata inherent in communicating.

End-to-end encryption on supported, versioned paths.

On supported, versioned message and file paths, content is encrypted at the endpoint before direct transfer or use of relay or rendezvous infrastructure. Relays forward ciphertext; unsupported, demo-only, and capability-dependent paths are documented separately, and internet discovery and availability still depend on deployed services.

Free and open source today.

There is no paid tier today. The AGPL-3.0 source is public, reviewable, buildable, and self-hostable. This page does not make an unverifiable promise about future pricing.

Try it right now

Inspect the pairing primitive in your browser.

This page runs both sides of the pairing primitive locally and renders its real invite QR plus five-word SAS. It is a cryptographic self-test, not an active pairing with your phone.

Verify these five words match across the local round trip.

orbit amber river candle harbor

The self-test creates fresh inviter and scanner state in this tab and confirms that both sides derive the same SAS and chain key. Real-device pairing additionally requires a second device, transport, user comparison, and the shipping application.

What just happened, under the hood
scope
Local one-tab Inviter/Scanner wrapper self-test; no phone, camera, daemon, or network transport.
key agreement
Ephemeral X25519 in the current ol_pair_qr path; no ML-KEM is used by this pairing wrapper.
signatures
Fresh local Ed25519 keys sign the pairing frames; no ML-DSA signature is produced here.
SAS + key
A five-word, 30-bit transcript SAS and a 32-byte chain key are derived and compared locally.
not included
No environmental field witness, durable identity, second-device proof, or human out-of-band comparison.
Where this is going

Connection that belongs to you.

The durable promise is the AGPL-3.0 right to inspect, run, modify, and share source. Privacy, availability, cost, and cryptographic properties still depend on the exact build, configuration, endpoints, transport, and providers.
